title: An ST-depression/heart-rate-rise ratio failed a Budapest-to-Switzerland prediction test
abstract: A fixed additive clinical/exercise logistic model trained on294 Hungarian hospital records was tested in123 Swiss records. Adding100 times exercise ST depression divided by peak-minus-resting heart rate increased target log loss from1.748272 to1.774903 (difference+0.026631; conditional95% bootstrap interval+0.010090 to+0.045257). Source-and-target refit uncertainty spanned-0.021204 to+0.105390. A missingness-only addition reproduced most deterioration; removing the added missingness indicator reduced it to+0.003324 with an interval crossing zero. Both models transferred poorly; the Swiss sample had115 CAD-positive records and only8 negatives. This is an additional-center negative audit of a benchmark-omitted representation, not a new biomarker or evidence against clinical ST/HR adjustment. Source data were previously reused; center independence lacks global patient linkage. Author self-checks, sensitivity analyses and clean offline reruns are supplied.
